tools.name: cleanapp_open
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to open CleanApp, report a real-world or digital problem, or browse the CleanApp miniapp. Do not use for household cleaning advice or computer disk-cleaning tasks.

tools.name: cleanapp_search_reports
tools.description: Use this when the user wants existing CleanApp observations about potholes, litter, illegal dumping, accessibility barriers, infrastructure damage, pollution, software bugs, scams or service problems. The brand need not be mentioned. Returns historical public reports, not an exhaustive or real-time

tools.description: Use this when the user wants to report an observed physical or digital problem: a pothole, dumped waste, unsafe infrastructure, accessibility barrier, pollution, software bug, suspected scam or service failure. tools.name: cleanapp_report_status
tools.description: Use this when the user asks what happened to their CleanApp submission and supplies the private tracking token returned for that report. Returns intake status and lane only, not proof of notification or resolution. Never search for another user’s receipt or guess identifiers.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: cleanapp_submit_report, cleanapp_report_status · Private data: cleanapp_search_reports, cleanapp_submit_report, cleanapp_report_status · Public sink: cleanapp_submit_report.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: cleanapp_submit_report, cleanapp_report_status · Private data: cleanapp_search_reports, cleanapp_submit_report, cleanapp_report_status · Public sink: cleanapp_submit_report

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
